title: Choose the mother universe backbone before further visual or subsystem implementation
research_summary: Code-level and runtime comparison of the verified MIT Your Eyes In Space commit e520568, current MIT Cosmos, and the current Personal Universe V2 composite. YEIS e520568 clean-builds, boots headlessly, covers hierarchical real+procedural universe navigation, floating origin/log depth, real HYG stars, deterministic systems, procedural planets, Earth/Moon/Mars imagery, Milky Way/deep universe and hand-made ExtraSystem exceptions. A research-copy patch exposing registerExtraSystem successfully injected HELION + AURORA-01 and rendered the Hero planet without modifying camera/render/system-generation internals. Its apparent 449 MB distribution is mostly optional lessons/tours media (~389 MB), which the personal site does not need. Cosmos has cleaner modular subsystems and stronger tests, but current main has SearchPanel type errors, relies on backend tile manifests for full data, and lacks an existing hand-made system override API. Current V2 has excellent customization and low local complexity but would require us to continue rebuilding cross-scale coordinates, real catalogs, surface streaming, deep-universe rendering and several mature subsystems already present in YEIS. Select a hybrid: reuse the exact MIT YEIS core as the universe/navigation/data/render backbone, preserve the current Astro/React personal-content shell and Hero-world override boundary, and retain ProceduralPlanets only as an optional renderer/fallback rather than the global engine.

sources.finding: Commit e520568 carries an MIT LICENSE and predates the later AGPL switch; it is a concrete reproducible permissive source boundary even though the advertised mit-final tag is not currently exposed.

The verified MIT snapshot contains hierarchical Universe/StarSystem models, deterministic procedural systems, HYG stars, galaxy/deep-universe renderers, floating-origin camera behavior, log-depth rendering, planetary imagery and ExtraSystem hand-made exceptions.

Cosmos is MIT and provides a modular browser universe engine with camera-relative coordinates, scale regimes, tile streaming, ephemerides, procedural materials, black-hole lensing and extensive tests, but its current data/backend integration is still in active development.
Solar Wanderer is a narrower MIT universe-scale travel implementation covering floating origin, log depth, JPL ephemerides and atmosphere, useful as a gap donor rather than a broader mother engine.
SpaceKit is an MIT astronomy/Three.js subsystem for ephemerides, Keplerian objects and orbital visualization; it is useful for isolated gaps but does not cover the whole personal-universe target.
ProceduralPlanets remains a strong MIT procedural-planet renderer already integrated locally, but its scope is planetary rendering rather than the cross-scale universe backbone.
three-nebula is a reusable MIT particle system for localized dust/nebula/effects, representative of component-level reuse that should only be considered after the mother engine decision.

search_ladder.conclusion: Two genuine browser-scale mother-engine candidates exist. YEIS e520568 is the only one that both clean-builds today and already implements the real+procedural+hand-made-exception model required by this site.
Solar Wanderer can donate cross-scale travel techniques if the chosen full solution has a gap, but adopting it as mother would still leave galaxy/catalog/deep-universe work.
Strong orbital and planet-generation subsystems exist, but continuing to compose them would reproduce a smaller version of capabilities already integrated in the verified YEIS mother candidate.
Particle/effect components remain available for future Hero-world or visual gaps, but they are downstream of the mother-engine choice.

coverage_matrix.decision: YEIS already ships a compact HYG-derived catalogue; Cosmos has the ingestion/tile architecture but current full catalogue ingestion is not the same ready-to-use path.
YEIS and current V2 both have deterministic generation; YEIS additionally connects it to the larger real/deep universe hierarchy.
Both external mothers materially exceed V2 here; this is not worth rebuilding locally.
Both external engines solve the multi-order-of-magnitude precision problem already; keeping V2 would require a new subsystem.
YEIS has this operating in a runnable complete product, while current V2 still uses discrete phase scenes.
YEIS already streams NASA Earth/Moon/Mars imagery and therefore removes another major future implementation branch.
All routes can cover procedural planets; this capability no longer differentiates the mother choice.

coverage_matrix.capability: Milky Way, galaxies and deep universe
coverage_matrix.decision: Both external mothers already extend beyond the local Milky Way prototype; V2 would need multiple new render/data layers.
A runtime PoC proved YEIS ExtraSystem can host HELION + AURORA-01 with one small public registration API; Cosmos needs a new plugin/entity abstraction.

coverage_matrix.capability: personal Astro/React content and custom Hero worlds
coverage_matrix.decision: Hybrid adoption deliberately keeps our shell/content/Hero boundary; a full YEIS fork would unnecessarily inherit simulator UI/branding.
YEIS e520568 and V2 clean-build. Cosmos packages and Vite bundle run, but current repo-wide TypeScript build fails on SearchPanel ApiEntity fields.
Cosmos visibly falls back when its star-tile manifest backend is absent; YEIS and V2 are static-site friendly.
YEIS exact commit is verified MIT, but the advertised mit-final tag is missing and HYG binary remains CC BY-SA; pin SHA and notices. Cosmos and local V2 are simpler license-wise.
The permissive YEIS snapshot is frozen because later upstream is AGPL; accept that cost only because its coverage substantially reduces our own implementation burden.

coverage_matrix.capability: payload can be trimmed for personal-homepage use
coverage_matrix.decision: YEIS apparent 449 MB dist is mostly optional lessons/tours; removing those leaves a much smaller astronomy/core payload while preserving notices and needed models/data.

candidates.name: Verified MIT YEIS core + current Astro/React personal shell + Hero override boundary
candidates.license: MIT source pinned to e520568; third-party data/assets retain NOTICE terms
candidates.reason: Highest whole-project leverage. Runtime PoC proves the existing ExtraSystem architecture can host our Hero world while the mother supplies the expensive astronomy, cross-scale coordinate, camera, rendering and data layers. Preserve our personal shell rather than its product UI.

candidates.name: Fork the entire verified MIT YEIS application and reskin it
candidates.license: MIT source pinned to e520568; third-party notices retained
candidates.reason: Technically viable and lowest migration effort, but it inherits simulator UI, lessons/tours/mission concepts and branding structure that conflict with the personal-universe product; stripping those after the fact is worse than reusing its core under our shell.

candidates.name: Cosmos engine under the current personal shell
candidates.reason: Excellent modular donor and likely future source for coordinate/tile/render techniques, but today it needs backend/data plumbing, has current TypeScript UI errors, and requires a new Hero-system plugin abstraction before it can replace V2 cleanly.

candidates.name: Continue the current V2 Galaxy Explorer + Helios + ProceduralPlanets composition as mother
candidates.source: local baseline 0b3be2a / composite of adopted registry subsystems
candidates.license: Project code plus MIT/ISC reused components
candidates.reason: Best immediate control but worst remaining-work profile. It would force us to build cross-scale precision, real surfaces, deeper catalog ingestion, ephemerides and deep-universe systems that the verified YEIS snapshot already has.

candidates.name: Solar Wanderer as scale/travel backbone
candidates.reason: Strong floating-origin/travel subsystem but narrower than the chosen mother; keep it as a future gap reference instead of layering another engine now.

candidates.name: SpaceKit orbital/ephemeris subsystem
candidates.reason: Useful isolated orbital tools but the selected mother already covers the immediate orbit/system need; adding it now would duplicate renderer/control responsibilities.

candidates.name: Retain ProceduralPlanets as optional Hero/fallback renderer
candidates.reason: Already integrated and useful for special Hero worlds or fallback baked planets, but no longer responsible for the universe backbone.

decision.rationale: Adopt the exact verified MIT YEIS e520568 source as the reusable universe core, not as the product UI. Keep the current Astro/React personal-content shell, reuse gate, Hero-world architecture and optional ProceduralPlanets renderer. Vendor only the needed MIT core/data/render pieces, preserve the upstream LICENSE/NOTICE and HYG CC BY-SA attribution, remove YEIS branding and optional lesson/tour media, and expose a narrow Hero-system registration adapter. This delivers the largest coverage gain while preserving our custom identity and avoiding a rewrite of mature cross-scale astronomy infrastructure.
decision.fallback: If the minimal YEIS-core extraction causes unacceptable coupling or bundle regressions, keep V2 as the shell/backbone and selectively port only YEIS Universe/StarSystem/Camera concepts under a fresh subsystem gate; Cosmos coordinate-utils remains the next donor.
